issue_text: classForCount() downgrades a "blocking"-classified finding to "warning" (non-blocking) when its severity is not critical/high (default branch, line 424-425). This severity gate directly drives gate verdicts: OpenBlockingCount, CountByClass().Blocking, and unresolvedBlockingFrom() all route through classForCount, and every task-done/pr-ready/epic-ready gate blocks on counts.Blocking > 0. Yet NO test in the findings package exercises a "blocking" classification at medium/low severity. The whole switch could be deleted (making every "blocking" finding block regardless of severity) or widened to `!= "low"` and the entire findings package test suite stays green — silently promoting medium-severity blocking findings to gate-closing blockers.

canonicalClass() aliases "blocker" -> "spec-contract" (line 403) and "followup" -> "follow-up" (line 409), plus the ReplaceAll("_","-") normalization (line 401). These aliases are gate-affecting: a finding classified "blocker" resolves to spec-contract which classForCount always treats as blocking. But no test anywhere feeds classification "blocker", "followup", or an underscore variant. Removing the "blocker" alias makes such a finding fall to default -> "warning" -> non-blocking, and every test still passes.
